result.effect: 5 independent loci reached genome-wide significance; no effect size printed

cells.quote: In SNP-based analysis, a total of 5 independent loci (LD-clumped at r2 threshold 0.01; MAF threshold = 0.05) reached genome-wide (GW) significance (p < 5e-08), filtered by imputation quality score (Rsq) > 0.3 and having at least 2 correlated SNPs (r 2 >0 . 5 ) w i t hp <1 e - 3 ( S u p p l e m e n t a r y Data 3/Table 1).
cells.note: The study reports genetic associations rather than a manipulated treatment comparison.

result.effect: PRS associated with 20 of 34 traits at FDR < 0.1; no effect size printed

cells.quote: All associations were in the expected direction (i.e., higher EA and CP PRS associated with better reading/language abilities).
cells.note: The reported association was stronger and more consistent for English-related phenotypes.

result.effect: PRS associated with 16 traits at FDR < 0.1 using clumping and thresholding; no effect size printed

cells.quote: All associations were in the expected direction (i.e., higher EA and CP PRS associated with better reading/language abilities).

O.outcome_detail: Reading comprehension, English vocabulary, English word reading and dictation

cells.quote: Higher ASD PRS were associated with better reading abilities.
cells.note: The study notes associations with several language phenotypes; this is not evidence that ASD-related genetics improves reading.

cells.quote: Most recently, a GWAS study with 1.1 million individuals identi ﬁed 1271 independent SNPs associated with educational attainment. 88 These SNPS were used to compute a polygenic prediction score that explained 11– 13% of the variance in educational attainment and 7 – 10% of the variance in cognitive performance in independent samples. 88
cells.note: The study reports a measured genetic association, not a manipulated educational treatment.

result.effect: R(2) ≈ 0.02%; approximately 1 month of schooling per allele

cells.quote: Critically, the estimated effects sizes of these three SNPs are small (coef ﬁcient of determination R(2) ≈0.02%; this equals approximately 1 month of schooling per allele). The relation between “years of education ” and the three SNPS from the original GWAS measuring “years of education ”70 was replicated several years later in a study that increased the sample size threefold.9
